work.text: It is his only signed work and has an unusual iconography for a painting of the Nativity.

It takes to an extreme the abandonment of consistent scale among the figures that had been a feature of Botticelli's religious paintings for some years, with the Holy Family much larger than the other figures, even those well in front of them in the picture space.

moment.text: Vasari's assertion that Botticelli produced nothing after coming under the influence of Savonarola is not accepted by modern art historians. The Mystical Nativity, Botticelli's only painting to carry an actual date, if one cryptically expressed, comes from late 1500,
infrared reflectography has shown that the original words on those ribbons correspond exactly to Savonarola's twelve privileges of the Virgin.

matters.text: This painting, at the end of the year 1500, in the troubles of Italy, I, Alessandro, in the half-time after the time, painted, according to the eleventh [chapter] of Saint John, in the second woe of the Apocalypse, during the release of the devil for three and a half years; then he shall be bound in the twelfth [chapter] and we shall see [him buried] as in this picture

matters.lead: Botticelli’s own inscription across the top of the canvas:

matters.text: Normally Botticelli used wood panels for his paintings. This painting is on canvas. Art historians suggest that perhaps for a painting with a dangerous message, canvas had the advantage that it could be rolled up and hidden.
